problem_statement: The shell command history must let the user browse previously entered commands with the up and down arrow keys. Pressing up repeatedly should step back through the commands in order, and once the oldest command has been shown, pressing up again must wrap around to the most recent command again; pressing down from the most recent command must reach the end. After a command is executed it must be stored, the most recent command must not be stored again if it is identical to the previous one, and when storage is full the oldest command must be evicted to make room for a new one.

verification.reason: The statement describes the behaviour but omits that the instance must be usable without an init call (the tests drop init and reset via purge) and leaves the wrap-around's intermediate 'no command' step ambiguous; both can be repaired by specifying the public interface and the exact observed wrap sequence.

problems.detail: The hidden tests remove every z_shell_history_init call and instead reset via a fixture that calls z_shell_history_purge, so the history must be fully usable after Z_SHELL_HISTORY_DEFINE without any separate initialization call. The statement never states this, so a solver could keep the init function (as the pre-PR code and existing tests do) and fail the hidden tests.

The new wrap-around test checks the exact sequence oldest -> no command (NULL,0) -> most recent -> ... The statement's 'pressing up again must wrap around to the most recent command again' can be read as the immediately-next up returning the most recent (skipping the empty step), which would not match the test; the intermediate 'no command' step is ambiguous.

leak_check.missing: The statement does not explicitly say that a command larger than the history capacity cannot be stored, nor does it mention purge behavior, both of which the tests exercise.

problem_statement_fixed: The shell command history must let the user browse previously entered commands with the up and down arrow keys. Pressing up repeatedly should step back through the commands in order, and once the oldest command has been shown, pressing up again must return no command and a further press must wrap around to the most recent command again; pressing down from the most recent command must reach the end. After a command is executed it must be stored, the most recent command must not be stored again if it is identical to the previous one, and when storage is full the oldest command must be evicted to make room for a new one. A history instance created with Z_SHELL_HISTORY_DEFINE must be fully initialized by the macro itself and usable immediately without any separate initialization call.
